display.title: Episode 1: The Two Voices
display.summary_short: The very first Tzivos Hashem on the Air: Uncle Yossi introduces the new show and its theme of achdus, leads the Shema, and tells "The Two Voices", a story about a dime on Shabbos.
display.summary_long: The premiere broadcast. Uncle Yossi welcomes children to their new radio program, promising stories, songs, marches, contests and prizes, and asks them to write in with requests. He explains that the show's main purpose is achdus, unity and togetherness, and that the first step is to do something together right now: everyone says the first lines of the Shema, in Hebrew and then in English. Story time brings "The Two Voices". On Shabbos afternoon little Sarah sees a dime on the road and hears two voices, the yetzer hara urging her to pick it up because it is "only a little sin" and the yetzer tov telling her not to. Her father explains with a parable about a rich man's heavy chandelier, held up by a chain tied in the attic, and a beggar who cut "just a little piece of rope". After a sponsor message, Uncle Yossi invites children to get a letter in the new children's Sefer Torah, to join the Tzivos Hashem club for a free wallet, ID card and Moshiach Times magazine, and to call the Dial-a-Jewish-Story line.
display.lesson: There is no such thing as a little sin: what looks small to us can be very big in Hashem's eyes, so listen to the yetzer tov.

date.note: First show; says 'tune in next week... next Tuesday'. One week before ep 2 (19 Kislev 5742 stated on air). Extrapolated, not bracketed.
